subject: history
title: The Golden Era 1924-29: How Stable?
welcome_lead: Today you'll stretch — was 1924-29 a Golden Era or just a calm before the storm?
meta_desc: GCSE History stretch — Stresemann era, Dawes Plan, culture and the limits of Weimar stability.
final_note: You can now judge how stable the Stresemann years really were.

concepts.def: 1924 US loans and easier reparations schedule
1929 US stock crash — US loans to Germany ended

walkthroughs.body_html:
Gustav Stresemann became Chancellor in 1923, then Foreign Minister until 1929.

He scrapped the old Mark, introduced the Rentenmark and called off passive resistance in the Ruhr. The economy began to recover with US loans.

The Dawes Plan (1924) and Young Plan (1929) eased reparations.

The Locarno Treaties (1925) accepted Germany's western borders. Germany joined the League of Nations in 1926. Berlin became a centre of culture — Bauhaus design, modern art and cabaret.

Strong answers see both sides. Yes — politics calmed, the economy grew and culture flourished.

But growth relied on US loans. Many farmers and small businesses missed out. Extremist parties stayed alive. When the Wall Street Crash hit in October 1929 — and Stresemann died the same month — the 'golden era' ended fast.

options: Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
The hyperinflation was caused by the Wall Street Crash.

mcqs.q: Why did the Treaty of Versailles cause resentment in Germany?
options: The hyperinflation was caused by the Wall Street Crash.
It assigned sole war guilt to Germany (Article 231) and imposed harsh reparations, territorial losses and military restrictions.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
Because Germany lost more soldiers than any other country in the war.

mcqs.q: How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.
Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
The hyperinflation was caused by the Wall Street Crash.
